questions: Should the Z-score normalization be computed column-wise (per column) or across the entire matrix as a single continuous sequence?
If column-wise normalization is used, should each column's mean and standard deviation be computed independently, or should the entire matrix's mean and standard deviation be used for all columns?
What should happen if a column has zero standard deviation (all identical values)? The clarification says NaN becomes 0.0, but is that the intended handling for uniform columns?
Should the input be strictly a 2D list/array, or can it be a pandas DataFrame or other iterable? The reference uses pd.DataFrame(matrix) directly.
Is the function expected to handle missing values (NaN) in the input matrix before normalization?
Should the output DataFrame preserve the original column and row indices, or use default integer indices?
What floating-point precision is expected for the normalized values? The reference uses scipy.stats.zscore which may produce double precision.
If the matrix has only one row or one column, should normalization still proceed? The reference handles single-element case.
